newsitem.title: FRANCE: USDA says EU wheat tax distorts trade.
newsitem.headline: USDA says EU wheat tax distorts trade.

text.p: A top official of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) said on Tuesday that a recent decision by the European Union to restore a tax on its wheat exports was a distortion of world markets.
But the official added that the United States was not planning to take any action in the near future, awaiting firmer data on the state of the new U.S. wheat crop.
"We see the tax as having the effect of distorting world markets signals. The problems we see with imposing the tax is that it encourages self-sufficient policies among food-importing

Riemenschneider, director of the grain and feed division of the USDA, told reporters during a grain conference here that there was a short-term benefit for the U.S. from the tax because it removed one key exporter from the world market.
But on the long term, the tax was distorting world trade because importers would be encouraged to produce more themselves in order to import less.
"There is very little action one can take in the U.S. until the new crop becomes available. The only action we can take is to voice our concern with EU officials," he said.

Last Thursday, the European Union re-imposed a tax on daily soft wheat exports in the face of volatile prices and concern over the prospects for world crops following a dry spell in Europe and frost in teh United States.
